question: Does the existing rule-only full-type static material candidate improve finite game utility over Unit on fresh generated 5x5 rules at a fixed paid budget?
changed_premise: Published PRIMARY static utility panels cover 4x4 and 6x6/8x8 but not 5x5. Published DEV_AUX105 reports a 5x5 cold-TD gain, which is not a static-price comparison and will not be duplicated.

rules.selection: All eight deterministic generated rules and every prespecified prefix are retained; no outcome- or feature-based filtering. No AUX rules/files or training outputs are reused.

roots.terminal_prefixes: Retain as zero-search terminal slots; do not replace.

arms.color_swap: Both candidate colors on each identical root/opponent pair. Candidate and foe checkpoints are fixed before any games.

outcomes.actual_terminal: Score the actual Core Session result.
outcomes.ongoing_after_96_candidate_plies: UNKNOWN; retain in finite bounds as [-1,1]. Do not convert to draw or extend the horizon.
outcomes.contrast: Within each fixed-foe/root/color-swapped pair, static_v2 candidate score minus Unit candidate score; report each foe separately, all seed-family values, finite bounds, UNKNOWN counts and actual nodes/caller time.
outcomes.decision: Strictly positive finite bounds against both foes retain static_v2 as a 5x5 candidate only. Nonpositive upper bounds against both de-prioritize it for this sampled 5x5 regime. Otherwise unresolved. No default, global price, training, population or strength claim.

cost.expected: 128 games; prior published 5x5 EVAL rate was about 1.97 seconds/game, suggesting about 4.2 minutes of game time plus setup and full record replay; budgeted below 40 minutes.
cost.cheaper_alternative: Profile/table-only comparisons verify support but cannot answer game utility, so they do not replace this bounded finite panel.

integrity: No training, solver, new worker, AUX checkout write or old panel refill.
Preserve promotion, drop, full Session history, repetition and real terminal results.
No seed replacement, rule filtering or outcome imputation.
